title: Separate response scales permitted ozone ranking reversals in North Wales domes in August-September 2021
abstract: We tested the equal response-scale assumption in an earlier ozone ranking result. We used 1,464 hourly records from a North Wales warming experiment in August and September 2021. Exact cumulative ratios give the heated relative response multiplier that first permits a positive contrast over all common non-increasing dry-air response shapes. At the two high ozone targets, the four primary thresholds were 1.0132 to 1.0503. Five of six primary witnesses kept every selected hour. Removing the brightest hour kept small high-target thresholds. Tested exponential response shapes needed larger high-target multipliers, from 1.5187 to 8.1073. All 60 cases passed an independent scalar check; 50 nonzero cases also matched linear programs. These are fixed-record sensitivity limits, not measured conductance or absorbed ozone. The records overlap earlier work and do not provide independent regional or yearly validation. One chamber per treatment, shared ambient weather, sensor uncertainty and unknown plant response limit inference. Original code, aggregate results, a figure and exact source hashes support reproduction. External source records stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Largest conditional heated-minus-ambient ozone summary over common non-increasing VPD response shapes as the heated response scale increases. Light is above 50. These are sensitivity frontiers, not measured uptake. Contains data supplied by UK Centre for Ecology & Hydrology.

citations.reason: Extends the equal-scale response ranking to a relative scale sensitivity test.
Provides the joint light and VPD comparison and motivates the brightest-hour omission.
Established the shared experiment exposure context.
